thread:
maria (PM): Heads-up: Large fintech wants a pricing path that separates latency-sensitive inference from bulk embedding workloads. They asked for a per-route add-on and usage caps per contract. Need to map product/contract changes.

jamal (Sales): They want 3 things: per-route enablement, hard monthly caps with overage blocking, and a differentiated SLA for the low-latency route. They'll sign if we can show clear billing and cap enforcement.

dev (Eng): Implementation options: 1) route-level flag + tagging + metering (low effort) 2) enforce hard caps at routing layer (more infra work) 3) priority lanes with preallocated tokens (complex). Which do we prioritize?

maria (PM): My proposal: ship route flags + soft caps (alerts + warnings) as V1, and hard caps + blocking for V2. GA criteria should include billing visibility and enforcement tests.

sara (Legal): Contract constraints: need to define "hard cap" semantics (what triggers blocking, refund/credit treatment), and add a clause for misuse/proof-of-billing disputes. Also define SLA boundaries when priority lane is used.

rachel (Solutions): Console UX: per-route toggle, expected monthly cost preview, and an override flow for account admins. Also need to show which models are eligible for priority lane (some big-context models not supported).

jamal (Sales): Fintech insists on blocking overages (they can't exceed regulatory budgets). They'll accept soft caps only as an interim demo but require hard cap in contract.

dev (Eng): Hard cap enforcement requires quota checks at request path with cheap check and fast failback message. Also need a tenant-level quota store and a durable counter for long windows. Estimate: soft caps = 1 sprint, hard caps = 4 sprints plus infra work.

maria (PM): Pricing packaging: Suggest add-on "Priority Route" priced as flat monthly + per-request multiplier. Caps offered as contract clause with two modes: soft (alerts) and hard (block + optional emergency override with audit).

sara (Legal): For emergency override, require admin auth + signed acknowledgment. We'll add a usage dispute window (30 days) and an audit trail requirement.

rachel (Solutions): For onboarding, we'll provide a migration guide: tag routes, simulate caps in sandbox, and validate traffic shaping. Also sample contract language for account teams.

launch-bot: flag:create "priority-route-v1" in staging; tests queued.

maria (PM): Launch criteria idea: 1) per-route tagging + billing shown in Console 2) soft-cap alerting + testable webhook 3) pilot signed with fintech and successful demo 4) legal template for cap clauses. GA adds hard-cap enforcement + SLA.

dev (Eng): One more constraint: priority lane must not degrade shared pool SLAs. We'll add isolation controls (rate limit headroom) in routing.

jamal (Sales): I'll close the loop with fintech and get signature for pilot. They want to see an admin override in demo. We should keep their pilot under NDA.

sara (Legal): I'll prepare two contract addenda: Pilot (AS-IS) and GA (SLA + cap enforcement).

maria (PM): Action items: Dev -> RFC for quota enforcement and timeline; Rachel -> Console mockups + estimator; Jamal -> pilot terms + NDA; Sara -> contract addenda drafts. Sync Monday 11am.

rachel (Solutions): I'll include sample copy for emergency override and admin audit logs.

jamal (Sales): Fintech confirmed Monday 4pm for pilot demo; asked if we can show soft-cap webhook firing.

maria (PM): OK keep Monday 11am internal sync, demo at 4pm. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
